<result>## Tooling note

**The `mcp__plugin_playwright_playwright__browser_*` tools are installed but non-functional on this machine** — every call fails with `Chromium distribution 'chrome' is not found at /opt/google/chrome/chrome`. Per the `### ui-review` section I fell back to throwaway Playwright scripts (written in the scratchpad, outside the repo) driving the bundled `chromium-1234`. All findings below come from a real browser against `npm run dev` on http://localhost:3000. I did not run `npx playwright test`.

I started the dev server and **stopped it again** (port 3000 is free for your verifier run). `git status` is byte-identical to what I found: `__tests__/styles/responsiveDashboards.test.ts`, `app/globals.css`, `e2e/travelguide.spec.ts`. I created one account to exercise favourites and reviews and deleted it; `userFavorite` and `review` are both back to 0. Note the DB already held 10 pre-existing `probe-*`/`payment-*` users before I arrived — not mine, and already inside your baseline.

**Headline: the 216px panel overlap is genuinely gone, at every width 320–1440, at rest and scrolled. But the overlap moved rather than disappearing — twice — and both new instances are invisible to a `.map`-vs-`.sticky-sidebar` rect test.**

---

## Blocking

### B1. `calc(100vh - 72px)` / `top: 72px` are wrong: the header is **89px**, and `position: sticky` never engages at all

`app/globals.css:521-524` and `:538-540`. Measured header heights across the sweep: **89px flat from 860 through 1440** (so, answering your specific risk: no, the header does *not* wrap anywhere between 900 and 1440). It wraps to 114.6px at 700–840 and 103px at ≤600 — both below the breakpoint, where `.map` no longer depends on the constant, so that part is harmless. The constant is simply wrong by 17px everywhere it is used.

Two consequences, both measured at 1440×900:

- `.guide` height is 828 and each panel is 828 → `stickySlackPx: 0`. A sticky box cannot move outside its containing block, so **both `position: sticky` declarations are inert.** The old `.guide` had `padding: 40px 20px`, which gave the map 80px of travel; `padding: 0` removed it. So the map does *not* stay put: wheeling over the sidebar scrolled its scrollport to its end (`sbScrollTop` 671 of 671) and then chained to the document, and the map's top went `89 → -149`.
- The panels are 17px taller than the space below the header (`sidebar.bottom = 917` vs `innerH 900`), so 17px of the sidebar's scrollport is below the fold at rest, and the header's `top: 72px` target sits 17px *above* the header's own bottom edge.

The visible result is bad. `desktop-1440x900-journey-02-sidebar-inner-scrolled.png`: the guide's prose scrolls up under the 75%-opaque, `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` header and is fully legible through it, colliding with the nav. You can read *"Detroit, also known as Motor City, is a city with a rich history and a vibrant cultural scene…"* running straight through **Flight Status**, **Check In**, the notification bell, the avatar and **Sign Out**. Two texts on top of each other, neither readable. That is the acceptance criterion's "overlap", relocated from panel-vs-panel to content-vs-header, and your rect test cannot see it.

### B2. Below 900px the map SVG overflows `.map` and bleeds into the Destinations panel

`app/globals.css:560-564` sets `height: 45vh; min-height: 260px` with no `overflow`, and `.map` is a plain block, so the aspect-locked `<svg>` (`viewBox="0 0 800 500"`, `width: 100%`) keeps its intrinsic height and spills past the box. Measured spill (`svg.bottom - map.bottom`):

| viewport | spill |
| --- | --- |
| 900×900 | **+157.5px** |
| 880×900 | +145 |
| 840×900 | +120 |
| 800×900 | +95 |
| 768×900 | +75 |
| **768×1024** | **+19.2** |
| 700×900 | +32.5 |
| ≤600 | negative (see M5) |

It paints *behind* the sidebar — `elementFromPoint` in the spill band returns `.sticky-sidebar` and `.guide-city-select`, so it does not block clicks — but the sidebar background is only 85% opaque, so it shows straight through. `stacked-900x900-state-map-overflow-into-list.png`: Mexico, Central America, Cuba, the Caribbean and the top of South America are clearly visible ghosting behind the **DESTINATIONS** heading and the New York / Los Angeles / Chicago rows. The new `border-top` divider reads as a seam drawn across the middle of the map rather than a boundary between two panels — which directly answers your question 2 about the divider: the rule is applied (`borderTopWidth: 1px`, `borderLeftWidth: 0`, confirmed) but at 700–900 it does not *function* as a boundary. `tablet-768x1024-state-map-overflow-into-list.png` shows the milder 19px version: a grey wedge of Colombia/Venezuela sitting below the line, above "DESTINATIONS".

Note the spill depends on viewport *height* too, so a short landscape tablet is worse than the 768×1024 you asked me to check.

### B3. Selecting a city produces no visible change at all in the stacked layout

`.guide-extra` renders *after* the 10-item list, so at stacked widths it is far below the fold and nothing scrolls it into view (`TravelGuideClient.tsx:65-70` — `selectCity` only sets state):

| viewport | action | `.guide-extra` top | in viewport |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 768×1024 | marker click | 1263.4 | **false** |
| 768×1024 | list click | 1263.4 | **false** |
| 390×844 | marker click | 1192.8 | **false** |
| 390×844 | list click | 1192.8 | **false** |

The `<h3>` does change to the right city (I verified "New York, USA" then "Miami, USA"), so it *says the true thing* — it just says it 1200px off-screen. A user taps a marker or a city row and the page appears not to respond; the only on-screen change is a 5–10px dot changing colour. At 390 you must scroll ~430px further to see the panel. At desktop it is marginal rather than broken: the detail top lands at 776 in a 900 viewport, so the "← All destinations / Favorite" row is just visible at the bottom edge. This is the single worst thing about the layout nobody has used before.

### B4. The city markers are Tab stop **209**, behind 202 unlabelled focus stops, 176 of them invisible

`react-simple-maps` renders every `<Geography>` as `<path tabindex="0">` with **no `aria-label` and no `role`**. Measured on `/travelguide`: `geoPaths: 202`, `focusablePaths: 202`, `allFocusable: 246`. Tabbing from the document start, the first city marker is reached at **hop 209** (hops 1–6 are the header links, 7–208 are country paths). Worse, **176 of the 202 paths lie entirely outside the SVG's visible viewport** and are clipped by the SVG viewport — identical count at 1440, 768 and 390, since the crop is viewBox-driven. So a keyboard user gets 176 focus stops on elements that cannot be seen, have no accessible name, and announce nothing.

This is pre-existing (the diff does not touch `Geographies`), but it is the direct answer to your question 5: **you cannot reach the markers by keyboard in any practical sense at any viewport**, and it belongs to the same acceptance criterion this slice closes ("without overlap or inaccessible content"). One incidental effect visible in `phone-390x844-keyboard-country-path-focus.png`: focus landing on a clipped element scrolled the header nav sideways, revealing that "Book Flight" is cut off (see M4).

The ring itself is fine once you get there: `3px solid rgb(192, 132, 252)`, `outline-offset: 2px`, `:focus-visible` matching — so `app/globals.css:768` works. It needs ~250ms to settle because of the global `* { transition: all 0.25s ease }`; my first measurement caught it mid-transition showing the UA white ring, which was my artefact, not a defect. Authoritative evidence is `*-keyboard-marker-focusring-zoom.png` (ignore `*-journey-11-marker-focus.png` and `*-state-keyboard-marker-focus.png`, taken with programmatic focus).

---

## High — the breakpoint and the framing (your questions 1 and 3rd risk)

### H1. 900 is too low: the row layout is already unusable well above it

`row-901x900-01-rest.png` answers this outright. At 901px the map column is 429×828 and the world map inside it is **429×268 — a postage stamp pinned to the top-left corner above 560px (68%) of empty gradient.** The whole eastern US is a smudge and the markers are 5px dots. It looks broken, not intentional. The empty band by width (`.map` height 828 throughout):

| width | svg height | empty below | % of panel empty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 901 | 268 | 560 | 68% |
| 1024 | 345 | 483 | 58% |
| 1120 | 405 | 423 | 51% |
| 1280 | 505 | 323 | 39% |
| 1440 | 605 | 223 | 27% |

Only around 1280–1440 does the row read as deliberate. So: 900 is the right *side* to stack on, but the wrong number — the row wants roughly 1100–1200, or `.map` wants to stop being a fixed `100vh − header` box holding a top-aligned aspect-locked SVG (centre it, and/or size the box from the SVG's aspect ratio).

### H2. Desktop 1440: legibly framed, not cropped or stretched — but centred on open ocean

`desktop-1440x900-01-rest.png`. The map fills 968×605 with no distortion (uniform viewBox scale, `preserveAspectRatio` default), no awkward crop of the subject, and 223px of soft-gradient letterbox below which reads acceptably because of `.map`'s radial gradient. So the answer to "legibly framed" is yes at 1440.

"Centred on something sensible" is a no. `projectionConfig={{ scale: 600, center: [-70, 28] }}` (`TravelGuideClient.tsx:134`) puts the centre in the Atlantic off the Bahamas, so all ten seeded cities cluster in the upper-left quadrant and the right ~55% is empty ocean. Los Angeles lands at x=21.3 at 1440 (the circle spans x 15–27, 15px from the viewport edge) and the Californian coastline is cropped off. There is an irony worth knowing: the 216px the old absolute sidebar covered was exactly that empty Atlantic on the map's right — so removing the overlap *exposed* the emptiest part of the frame, and the map looks emptier now than it did broken. Moving the centre west (roughly `[-95, 38]`) and/or raising the scale would make the frame match its content. Not a regression; a presentation follow-up.

### H3. Marker hit targets fail WCAG 2.5.8 at every viewport, badly at phone

`r={5}` in viewBox units scales with the map width. Measured rendered diameters: **12.1px at 1440, 9.6px at 768, 4.875px at 390** (selected marker 19.4 / 15.4 / 7.8). WCAG 2.5.8 AA wants 24×24. I could only click them with a synthetic precise/`force` click — a finger cannot hit a 4.9px dot, so the practical answer to "can you see and click the city markers" at 390 is: see, barely; tap, no. This is an *improvement* on the prior state (the map computed to width 0 at 390, so markers did not exist, and were 3.2px at 768), so it is not a regression — but this slice is the one claiming mobile widths work, so a hit-target floor belongs in scope or in an issue.

---

## Medium — pre-existing, reached by this journey, worth filing rather than fixing here

### M4… ordered by severity:

**M1. The rating `<select>` is white text on the UA light default — ~1.2:1.** `#review-rating` computes `color: rgb(255, 255, 255)` over `background-color: rgb(239, 239, 239)`, `appearance: auto`. "★★★★★ Excellent" is invisible at every viewport. See `phone-390x844-state-review-form-select-contrast.png` and the desktop equivalent. `app/globals.css:707-727` styles the label and textarea but never the select. Hard blocker for the review journey, untouched by this diff.

**M2. `.guide-map-state` lands top-left in a large empty panel** — your second risk, confirmed. Error state at 1440: rect `(0, 89)–(968, 161)`, `text-align: start`, one 60%-white italic line with ~750px of unexplained black beneath it (`desktop-1440x900-state-map-error.png`). It reads as a broken page rather than graceful degradation. Centring it in `.map` (which now needs to become a flex/grid container anyway for B2/H1) fixes both at once. Its contrast is fine — `rgba(255,255,255,0.6)` over the dark panel is ≈7:1, passes AA. The message text itself is correct and `role="status"` is present.

**M3. "Loading map…" never appears once hydrated.** With `/map.json` hanging: `svgPresent: true`, `geoPaths: 0`, and **no `.guide-map-state` element at all** — ten unexplained coloured dots on a black gradient (`phone-390x844-state-map-loading.png`). `Geographies` fetches in an effect and does not suspend, so the `Suspense` fallback at `TravelGuideClient.tsx:131` can never fire; the SSR copy at `:128` only covers hydration. So the string describes hydration, not map loading. The change makes this more prominent because the panel is now full-bleed. Pre-existing.

**M4. Header nav clips at ≤600px.** At 390 the last `<li>` ("Sign Up") has a right edge of 441 against a 390 client width, `documentElement.scrollWidth` is still 390 (so no page scroll exposes it), and focusing it scrolls the nav sideways instead. Off-screen and unreachable at rest — visible in `phone-390x844-01-rest.png` (Sign Up absent) versus `phone-390x844-keyboard-country-path-focus.png` (Sign Up present, "Book Flight" now cut). Outside `.guide`, pre-existing, but it is the same acceptance criterion.

**M5. Dead band below the map at ≤600px.** Same root cause as B2, opposite sign: at 390 the svg is 243.8 tall in a 379.8 box, so **136px (36%) of `.map` is empty gradient** before the divider, pushing the list down for nothing (`phone-390x844-01-rest.png`). The crossover from spill to dead band is around 620px at a 900-tall viewport.

## Nothing to report under these headings — verified, passing

- **The original defect is fixed.** `.map` and `.sticky-sidebar` rectangles never intersect at 320/390/768/900/901/1024/1440, at rest and at page bottom. Both panels have non-zero width and height, and `sidebar.left ≥ 0` everywhere — the −82px case is gone.

Keyboard `Enter` on a marker selects (Seattle). Nothing that worked at desktop broke, and it all functions stacked — subject to B3, which is about feedback, not function.
- **Console is completely clean.** Zero errors and zero warnings across the whole signed-in journey at all three viewports. No ResizeObserver loop warnings, no D3 warnings, no React hydration or key warnings. Your fourth risk found nothing.
- **Below 900 both panels are `static`** (`mapPos: "static"`, `sbPos: "static"`, `overflowY: visible`) and the page scrolls as one piece with no pinning — the second half of your question 4 passes.
- **Above 900 the sidebar does scroll inside itself** (`sbScrollH 1499` / `sbClientH 828`) — the first half of question 4 passes for the sidebar; it fails for the map (B1).

## What your Playwright layout test cannot catch

Worth saying explicitly since it passes at all seven widths and three of my four blocking findings are inside its blind spot: it measures `.map`'s box, not the `<svg>` inside it (B2); it measures the two panels against each other, not against the sticky header (B1); and it measures geometry, not whether a state change is visible (B3). If you want geometry to hold the line on B2, the assertion needs to be `.map svg`'s rect against `.sticky-sidebar`'s, or `.map`'s `scrollHeight` against its `clientHeight`.

gh issue create --title "Travel guide map is framed on open ocean, cropping Los Angeles at the viewport edge" --label roadmap --body 'Found while closing #78'"'"'s responsive residue, and verified against the running app in Chromium at 390, 768, 901, 1024 and 1440.

## Where

`components/ui/TravelGuideClient.tsx` — the `ComposableMap` projection config:

```tsx
projection="geoEqualEarth"
projectionConfig={{ scale: 600, center: [-70, 28] }}
viewBox="0 0 800 500"
```

## What was observed

`center: [-70, 28]` is in the Atlantic off the Bahamas. All ten seeded cities therefore cluster in the upper-left quadrant and roughly the right 55% of the frame is empty ocean. At 1440 the Los Angeles marker lands at x=21.3 with its circle spanning x=15–27 — **15px from the viewport edge** — and the Californian coastline is cropped off entirely.

There is an irony worth recording: the 216px that the old absolutely-positioned sidebar covered was precisely that empty Atlantic on the map'"'"'s right. Fixing the overlap in #78 therefore *exposed* the emptiest part of the frame, so the map now looks emptier than it did while it was broken. That makes this a presentation defect made visible by a correctness fix, not a regression introduced by one.

## Why it matters

The map is the primary way to choose a destination. A frame centred on water, with the westernmost city touching the edge, makes the ten destinations look like an accident of projection rather than a set of places the airline flies. Roughly `center: [-95, 38]` with a raised scale would frame the actual content.

## Not fixed in #78'"'"'s slice

That slice fixed geometry — panel overlap, drawing overflow, breakpoint. Choosing what the map is centred on is a design decision about which places are framed and how prominently, and it changes what every visitor sees. It deserves its own change rather than riding along in a layout fix.

Note the seeded city set is hand-maintained in `lib/data/CityGuideData.ts`, so whoever picks this up should choose the centre and scale from that data rather than from the ten rows that happen to exist today.' 2>&1 | tail -2

input.command:
gh issue create --title "Travel guide city markers are a 4.9px tap target at phone width" --label roadmap --body 'Found while closing #78'"'"'s responsive residue. Measured in Chromium against the running app.

## Where

`components/ui/TravelGuideClient.tsx` — the city `Marker` circles use `r={5}` (and `r={8}` when selected) in viewBox units, so they scale with the map width.

## What was observed

Rendered diameters:

| viewport | unselected | selected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1440 | 12.1px | 19.4px |
| 768 | 9.6px | 15.4px |
| 390 | **4.875px** | 7.8px |

WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) asks for 24x24 CSS pixels unless an exception applies. No exception does here: the markers are not inline in a sentence, and there is no equivalent alternative control that is large enough — the Destinations list is an alternative *route* to the same outcome, which arguably satisfies 2.5.8'"'"'s "alternative" exception, so this may be a near-miss rather than a failure. Worth a judgement from someone who wants to argue it either way.

Either way, a 4.9px dot cannot be hit with a finger. In the rendered review the markers could only be clicked with a synthetic precise click; the practical position at 390 is that you can just about see them and cannot tap them.

## Why it matters, and why it is not a regression

Before #78 the map computed to **zero width** below 512px, so at phone width the markers did not exist at all, and at 768 they were 3.2px. So this is strictly an improvement. But #78'"'"'s acceptance criterion is that the guide "works at supported desktop and mobile widths", and a map whose only interactive elements cannot be tapped is a weak reading of "works" — so it belongs on the record rather than being left implicit.

## Suggested direction

The marker radius could scale inversely with the map width so the rendered size stays constant, or each marker could carry a larger transparent hit circle with the visible dot drawn inside it. The second is the smaller change and keeps the visual design as it is.

Note that hit-testing itself is correct — `elementFromPoint` at each marker centre returns the `circle.guide-marker` with its `aria-label` at all viewports, so nothing obstructs them. This is purely about size.' 2>&1 | tail -2

Verified against the running app by hanging the `/map.json` request. ## Where `components/ui/TravelGuideClient.tsx` — the map panel has two states that look like they cover loading: - a server-rendered / pre-hydration branch that renders `.guide-map-state` with "Loading map…" or the failure message - a `Loading map…

}>` around `` ## What was observed With `/map.json` never resolving, the rendered page has `svgPresent: true`, `geoPaths: 0`, and **no `.guide-map-state` element at all** — ten coloured city dots floating on a black gradient with nothing saying why the world is missing. The reason is that `Geographies` fetches its topology in an effect and does not suspend, so the `Suspense` fallback can never fire. The pre-hydration branch only covers the window before hydration, not the window while the topology is in flight. So the "Loading map…" string describes hydration, not map loading, and the honest loading state does not exist. There *is* a working failure path — a HEAD probe of `/map.json` sets `mapFailed` and renders "The map could not be loaded. Choose a destination from the list instead." — but a request that hangs rather than fails, or one that fails after the probe succeeded, lands in the gap above. ## Why it matters #78 delivered "provide meaningful empty, loading, and map-failure states" and the failure state does work. This is the loading half, and the fix in #78'"'"'s layout slice made it more prominent rather than less: the map panel is now full-bleed and correctly sized at every width, so the empty state occupies a large, well-framed area instead of a mis-sized one. ## Suggested direction `Geographies` accepts a render prop that receives the parsed geographies, so the component already knows when the list is empty. Rendering the status message when `geographies.length === 0` after hydration would close the gap without adding state. Whoever does it should decide whether an indefinitely hanging fetch should eventually become the failure state rather than a permanent "loading".' 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Three issues filed. Status while the code review runs:

**ui-review's headline was that the 216px panel overlap is genuinely gone — but the overlap had *moved* rather than disappeared, twice, in ways my rect test structurally could not see.** That was the most valuable thing it told me, and it was right both times:

- **The header is 89px, not the 72px hard-coded in four places.** That 17px error put part of the panels below the fold and aimed `position: sticky` above the header's own bottom edge. Worse, removing the old `padding: 40px 20px` removed the sticky slack that padding had accidentally provided — so the sidebar's internal scroll chained to the document and dragged the whole guide up under the translucent header, with city prose legible *through* the nav labels. Fixed with a single measured `--header-height` token and `overscroll-behavior: contain`.
- **Below the breakpoint the map SVG overflowed its panel** by up to 157px, painting through the 85%-opaque sidebar so Cuba and the Caribbean ghosted behind the DESTINATIONS heading. `.map` is now a clipping, centring box with the SVG fitted to it — which also fixes the 136px dead band at phone width and the map-status text stranded in a corner.

Two more it caught that geometry can't express: **selecting a city produced no visible change when stacked** — the detail panel sits ~1200px below the fold, so tapping a marker changed a 5px dot and nothing else. And **202 unlabelled focusable country paths**, 176 of them clipped outside the viewBox, putting the first city marker on tab stop **209**. Both fixed; the second is squarely "inaccessible content" under #78's own criterion.

It also showed my breakpoint choice was wrong: at 901px the map draws the world **429×268 in an 811-tall panel — 68% empty**. Raised to 1100, where the row reads as deliberate.

**Writing tests for those fixes surfaced two more defects of my own.** A city is selected on mount via `DEFAULT_CITY_NAME`, so my scroll-into-view effect scrolled the page on load — caught by a test asserting it doesn't. And `tsc` caught that I passed a `userId` prop the component doesn't accept: 15 Jest tests passed happily, because types are stripped. That's the second slice in a row where the typecheck caught something no test could.

**Eight mutants, all dead** — each restoring one specific fix, including two that only die against the styles guard because they're judgement calls geometry can't adjudicate (the breakpoint number, and scroll chaining).

Scrolling from the click handler (or tracking a "selection request" counter rather than the name) covers it.

The `hasSelectedOnce` ref guard is defeated by React Strict Mode's double effect invocation, so in dev the page does scroll itself on load.** Strict Mode is on by default for the App Router and nothing disables it in `next.config.mjs`. The user sees a panel they cannot interact with by keyboard, and the next `Tab` scrolls the viewport back up to the following marker. Moving focus to the panel (`detailRef.current.focus()` with `tabIndex={-1}`) instead of only scrolling would keep focus and viewport together, and would also announce the change to a screen reader.

Closes the last remaining piece of #78 (P3.1 Repair travel-guide presentation): its **first** acceptance criterion, that the guide "works at supported desktop and mobile widths without overlap or inaccessible content". Its other five tasks were delivered by #141 / `74b8dec` — this issue has been stale rather than unstarted, which a triage pass established before this work began.

## The defect, with the arithmetic

`<div className="guide page-container">` means `.guide` and `.page-container` are the **same element**, so the guide inherited `flex-direction: column`, `align-items: center` and `padding: 40px 20px`. Two rules then disagreed about which box they were measuring against:

- `.map` took `width: calc(100% - 472px)` and, being centred, sat with its left edge at a constant `20 + 472/2 = 256` and its right edge at `W - 256`.
- `.sticky-sidebar` was `position: absolute; right: 0`, so its left edge was at `W - 472` against the *padding* box.

Overlap = `(W - 256) - (W - 472)` = **216px at every width**. Predicted algebraically, then measured at exactly 216px at both 768 and 900. Below 512px the map's width computed negative and clamped to zero, and the sidebar's left edge reached **−82px** at 390 — unreachable, because an absolute box with a negative offset does not extend the scroll region. There was no `@media` rule anywhere targeting these three selectors, in a stylesheet with eight breakpoints for other surfaces.

Both panels are now in normal flow, so neither can be positioned over the other.

## Removing the overlap moved it twice

A rendered review caught both, and neither was visible to the geometry test I had written:

- **The header is 89px, not the 72px hard-coded in four places.** That 17px error put the panels past the fold and aimed `position: sticky` at a line above the header's own bottom edge. Worse, the old `padding: 40px 20px` had been *accidentally supplying the sticky slack* — with `padding: 0` there was none, so reaching the end of the destinations list chained its scroll to the document and dragged the whole guide up under the translucent header, with city prose and nav labels legible through one another. Now one measured `--header-height` token, and `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the sidebar.
- **The map SVG overflowed its panel by up to 157px**, painting through the 85%-opaque sidebar so that Cuba and the Caribbean ghosted behind the DESTINATIONS heading. It is aspect-locked and keeps its intrinsic height whatever the panel says. The panel now clips and centres it — which also removes 136px of dead gradient at phone width and puts the map's status messages in the middle of the panel instead of alone in its top-left corner.

## The breakpoint moved from 900 to 1100

900 was my first choice because the stylesheet already breaks there. It was too low: at 901px the map column is 429px and draws the world **429×268 inside an 811-tall panel — 68% of the panel empty**, the eastern United States a smudge, markers 5px dots. Stacked, the same viewport draws it 648×405. The row only reads as deliberate from about 1100 up.

| width | map column | panel empty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 901 | 429 | 68% |
| 1024 | 552 | 58% |
| 1100 | 628 | 52% |
| 1440 | 968 | 27% |

## Two things geometry cannot see

- **Stacked, choosing a city changed nothing visible.** The detail panel renders below a ten-item list, about 1200px past the fold; the heading said the right thing 1200px away and the only on-screen change was a five-pixel dot. It is now revealed from the click handler with focus following. Not from an effect keyed on the selection, which got it wrong three ways: re-selecting the *already selected* city — `DEFAULT_CITY_NAME` on every fresh load, so the likeliest first tap on a phone — sets identical state and React bails out, so nothing ran; a ref guard meant to skip the mount is defeated by Strict Mode's double invocation, because refs survive the simulated remount, so the page scrolled itself on arrival in development; and an effect cannot tell a selection the customer asked for from one the component chose for them. `scroll-margin-top` keeps the panel clear of the header, because `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` *start*-aligns an element taller than the scrollport — so "nearest" parked the panel's back and favourite controls underneath a `z-index: 1000` header where they could not be clicked.
- **`react-simple-maps` renders every country as a focusable `path` with no accessible name and no role.** 202 of them, 176 clipped outside the viewBox, so the first city marker was **tab stop 209** behind 202 stops that announce nothing and cannot be seen. They are decoration; the markers are the controls. I confirmed against `react-simple-maps@3.0.0` that it spreads `restProps` *after* its hard-coded `tabIndex: "0"`, so the override lands.

Also fixed: the review **rating select had no CSS rule at all**, so it inherited white text onto the user agent's light control background — about **1.2:1**, invisible, in the one control the review journey cannot be completed without.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npm run lint` | clean |
| `npm run test:unit` | 95 suites / **1082 tests** (baseline on `main`: 95 / 1069) |
| `npm run test:database` | 44 suites / 324 tests, unchanged and run separately |
| `npm run build` | clean; sanitize step ran |
| `npx playwright test` | **56/56** (46 before; the layout test runs 10 widths) |
| `npm audit` / container scan | not reachable — no dependency, `Dockerfile`, standalone or sanitize change |

No migration in this slice.

The red step was a real one: the layout test asserts the two panels' rectangles **never intersect**, which is layout-agnostic — a row and a stacked column both satisfy it, so it cannot be passed by a fix that merely relocates the overlap. All seven original widths failed before the change and pass after.

## Mutation testing — 18 mutants, all dead

Five in the first round, each restoring one part of the original defect; eight for the rendered-review fixes; five for the code-review fixes. Two found something:

- **D5 survived**: leaving the stacked map `position: sticky`. Sticky participates in normal flow, so it stacks correctly *at rest* and only pins itself over the sibling once the page moves — and I was measuring at scroll position 0 only. The test now measures at rest **and** scrolled to the bottom, and D5 dies at exactly the four stacked widths.
- **D3 survived the rendered check and dies against the styles guard**: restoring `width: calc(100% - 472px)` on the map. With the sidebar now a flex item that calc computes the same result, so it is redundant duplication rather than a behavioural difference — the guard is what stops two numbers that must agree being reintroduced as a pair.

Three mutants are killable only by the styles guard, and that is the honest place for them: the breakpoint number, the scroll-offset ceiling and `overscroll-behavior` are judgement calls that geometry cannot adjudicate.

## Two defects of my own that the tests caught

- A city is selected on mount, so my first version of the reveal **scrolled the page on load**, moving it under a visitor who had asked for nothing. Caught by a test asserting it does not.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` caught that I passed a `userId` prop `TravelGuideClient` does not accept. **All 15 Jest tests passed**, because types are stripped. Second slice in a row where the typecheck caught something no test could.

## One review finding I could not substantiate

An earlier rendered review reported the sticky header as having no `backdrop-filter`. The rule is at `app/globals.css:64`; the `backdrop-filter: none` at line 292 is on the search-form inputs. What it saw is the intended frosted-glass treatment used consistently across the app, so I have not filed it.

## Filed and not fixed

- **#316** — the map is framed on open ocean (`center: [-70, 28]`), cropping Los Angeles 15px from the viewport edge. *Exposed* rather than caused by this change: the 216px the old sidebar covered was exactly that empty Atlantic, so the map looks emptier now than it did while broken. Choosing what the map is centred on is a design decision.
- **#317** — city markers are a 4.9px tap target at 390px (12.1px at 1440). Strictly an improvement, since the map had zero width below 512px before, but worth recording against a slice that claims mobile widths work.
- **#318** — "Loading map…" can never appear, because `Geographies` fetches in an effect and does not suspend, so a hanging fetch shows ten unexplained dots.

The reviewer also observed the header nav clipping at ≤600px, which is already **#311**.

## Known limits of what is pinned

`--header-height: 89px` is frozen, and the header's real height depends on whether its logo and page title wrap — about 115px between 700 and 840, about 103px at or below 600. No rule that uses it is evaluated at a width where it is wrong, since the guide stops depending on it below 1100. The scroll offset is a deliberate **ceiling** (120px) rather than a measurement, because the error is asymmetric: too large costs a little space, too small parks controls under the header. The e2e spec asserts the offset stays at or above the header *as measured on that render* rather than asserting either number, so a webfont swap cannot fail it while blaming the panels. Measuring the header at runtime and publishing it as a custom property would remove the frozen number altogether; that is a larger change than this slice.

content.text:
**#78 is closed.** Merged as `1e6b456`, branch deleted, and the issue closed with a task-by-task record showing it was stale rather than unstarted — five of its six items were already delivered by #141.

## What the fix actually was

The overlap was **216px at every width**, and the cause was two rules disagreeing about which box they measured against: `.guide` shares its element with `.page-container`, so it inherited `flex-direction: column`, `align-items: center` and `padding: 40px 20px`. That centred the map at `W − 512` wide while the absolutely-positioned sidebar measured from the padding box. I derived `(W − 256) − (W − 472) = 216` algebraically and then measured exactly 216px at 768 and 900. Below 512px the map clamped to zero width and the sidebar's left edge reached **−82px**, unreachable.

**But removing the overlap moved it twice rather than ending it**, and the rendered review caught both in ways my geometry test structurally could not:

- The header is **89px, not the 72px hard-coded in four places** — and the old padding had been *accidentally supplying the sticky slack*, so with `padding: 0` the sidebar's scroll chained to the document and dragged the guide under the translucent header.
- The map SVG **overflowed its panel by up to 157px**, painting through the 85%-opaque sidebar.

Then the code review found a genuine CSSOM subtlety: `scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` **start**-aligns an element taller than the scrollport, so "nearest" parked the panel's back and favourite controls at y=0 under a `z-index: 1000` header where they couldn't be clicked.

## The parts worth remembering

My reveal-on-selection went through three wrong shapes before landing. An effect keyed on the selection never ran when you re-selected the already-selected city — which is `DEFAULT_CITY_NAME` on every fresh load, so the likeliest first tap on a phone. A ref guard meant to skip the mount is defeated by Strict Mode's double invocation, because refs survive the simulated remount. Moving it to the click handler removed the whole class of problem: a handler runs exactly when somebody acts.

**Two defects of my own, caught by tests rather than by me:** the first version scrolled the page on load, and `tsc` caught a `userId` prop the component doesn't accept while all 15 Jest tests passed happily. That's the second slice running where the typecheck found something no test could.

**18 mutants, all dead.** Two found real gaps — D5 showed I was measuring at scroll position 0 only, so a sticky panel that stacks correctly *at rest* and pins itself over its sibling on scroll went unseen; D3 survives the rendered check and dies only against the styles guard, which is the honest place for it.

Three follow-ups filed: **#316** (map framed on open ocean, cropping LA — exposed rather than caused by this, since the 216px the sidebar hid was exactly that empty Atlantic), **#317** (4.9px tap targets at phone width), **#318** ("Loading map…" is unreachable).

**Next**, per the triage: the destructive-button pass (**#250** → **#290**), where the intent is already in the code and silently overpainted by `globals.css:417` — one shared root cause, and #250 establishes a class #290 reuses. After that the notification drawer bundle (**#209** + **#210** remainder + **#241**), which is one component and the largest of the three.
